subject: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Bradley —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I took another pass with our pricing and delivery teams. We can match the headline economics you shared from ScaleRun at the unit level for the first 12 months, plus a set of technical carveouts to reduce your migration risk.

High level offer (summary attached):
- Unit price parity vs ScaleRun for compute + embeddings for 12 months
- One-time migration credit of $90k applied to onboarding and integration work
- SLA fallback appendix: accelerated response windows and a 15% credit for sustained latency breaches over agreed SLOs
- Technical carveouts: guaranteed KV-cache export, muscle on private VPC peering, and a short-term runbook for model quantization validation

Open asks from our side to finalize:
1) Agreement that production can start on our Dedicated tier (not hosted) for at least the first 90 days for data isolation.
2) Confirmation of two integration milestones we can tie the credit to (pilot ingest + first 1M tokens).
3) Any legal must-haves from your side (NDA/additional clauses).

Attaching the TCO workbook and a short parity term PDF — Irene included the SLA appendix draft. If this looks good, can we lock a call Monday to sync legal and engineering?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.com)

Attachments: FinEdge_Migration_TCO_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Parity_Term_Summary.pdf, SLA_Fallback_Appendix.docx

From: Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Park <anna.park@finedge.com>, legal@finedge.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Jordan —

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the detail. A few quick clarifications before we loop legal:
- The parity unit price looks reasonable, but ScaleRun's offer includes a 9-month ramp credit tied to usage growth. Can Redwood match that duration or provide an equivalent staged credit?
- For the migration credit: can $90k be split 50/50 between pre-go-live professional services and post-go-live performance validation? Our PSC will want to see that the vendor stays accountable through the first 60 days.
- The Dedicated tier requirement is fine, but we need clear egress limits and an estimate of network fees for the VPC peering — our infra team flagged potential egress costs.

Also attaching a short checklist from our procurement team (see comment inline). Let's aim for the Monday call — but can you do an earlier slot on Friday?

Thanks,
Brad
Bradley Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
FinEdge Systems

Attachment referenced: FinEdge_Procurement_Checklist.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Bradley —

Thanks — quick responses inline:  
1) Staged credit: We can shift the $90k into a 9-month ramp schedule: $40k up front, then $50k spread across months 3–9 contingent on usage tiers. We'll reflect it in the deal worksheet.
2) Split allocation: Yes — 50/50 split between PS and post-go-live validation is acceptable. We'll tie the second half to the milestone of 1M validated tokens and a signed post-mortem of the pilot run.
3) Egress/network: Our infra team modeled a conservative estimate — see Tab "Network" in the TCO workbook (summary: ~ $2.5k/mo on average for the pilot, with a 95th percentile cap we can set at $7k). We'll add a line item for actual egress reconciliation.

We can do Friday 10:00am PT for a 30-minute sync if that works for your team. We'll have Irene on for the SLA appendix and Lauren for the commercial sheet.

Jordan

On Thu, Jun 19, 2025 at 09:14 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Bradley —
>
> Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation...

From: Anna Park <anna.park@finedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Jordan/Irene/Brad —

Quick note from procurement/legal: any parity commitment needs a clear definition of what is 'equivalent' — ScaleRun's offer included a 1:1 trained-model migration promise and a 75-day rollback window. Can Redwood confirm whether model artifact portability and a rollback SLA are covered in your carveouts? Our legal also wants to see a sample sideletter for the 9-month credit.

Thank you,
Anna Park
Procurement Manager
FinEdge Systems

Cc: legal@finedge.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@finedge.com>, Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Anna/Bradley —

Couple concrete datapoints to address legal's asks: 
- Model portability: Redwood will provide a KV-cache export and a model artifact snapshot process during the migration window; we will not retain copies after export per agreed contract language. This is operationally tested in our Dedicated-to-Private runbooks.
- Rollback SLA: We can commit to a 75-day rollback window aligned to your comment, with a documented rollback plan and a single-point engineering contact during the window. We will add an explicit fallback credit schedule if rollback extends beyond an agreed threshold.
- Sideletter: Lauren has prepared a drafter sideletter for the 9-month staged credit (attached as part of the commercial packet).

If that looks acceptable, Jordan and I propose the Friday 10:00am PT call to finalize the sideletter and the egress reconciliation approach.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
(irene.choi@redwood.com)

Attachment referenced: Redwood_Parity_Term_Summary.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna.park@finedge.com>, Bradley Chen <bradley.chen@finedge.com>, legal@finedge.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial parity proposal & deployment carveouts for FinEdge migration

Team —

Great sync today. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 
- Commercial: Redwood to provide a 9-month staged credit schedule (details in HS-43219). Payment schedule: $40k at contract signature; remaining $50k unlocked by usage milestones across months 3–9.
- Technical: We will deliver KV-cache export tooling and an artifact snapshot runbook during the migration cutover. Rollback window confirmed at 75 days; Redwood SRE will be on-call for the first 14 days post-cutover.
- SLA: Included fallback credits in the appendix; legal to review sideletter and return with redlines by Wednesday COB.
- Ops: Egress cap set to $7k/mo during pilot; any overages reconciled monthly.

Action items assigned: 
- Lauren: send final sideletter draft and commercial worksheet by EOD Tuesday.
- Irene: attach the rollback runbook and validate KV export steps with your infra team by Tuesday.
- Bradley/Anna: loop legal and confirm preferred signature flow (DocuSign or shared counter-signed PDF).

If there are no surprises, we'll convert the commercial worksheet to a term sheet Wednesday and target signature next week.

Thanks — moving quickly on this is important for both teams.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.com)
